newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco surveys food production, population growth.
newsitem.headline: Morocco surveys food production, population growth.

text.p: Morocco, a major wheat importer, could meet 50 percent of its cereal needs even in drought, according to a report by government experts working under the supervision of the Agriculture Ministry.
Details of the report, being submitted to the FAO summit in Rome, were carried on Wednesday by the official Moroccan news agency MAP.
A catastrophic drought in the 1994/95 season meant Morocco imported 2.5 million tonnes of wheat, plus other cereals, with domestic production covering only 21 percent of the demand.

With the population increasing at an annual average 1.55 percent, to reach 40 million people by the year 2020, the report said Moroccan farm output could exceed demand in some areas but fall behind in others.
It said wheat, sugar and red meat production would grow at a lower rate than population, while edible oils, white meat, eggs, milk and milk products would grow faster.

"The level of cover of demand by national production could (in a drought year) be around 50 percent for cereals, between 77 and 90 percent for (edible) oils, 62 percent for milk and 50 to 58 percent for red meat," the report said.
To achieve this, more state funds were needed for improving the land, for training and research, MAP quoted the report as saying.
Between 1990/91 and 1994/95 seasons, useable farming land reached around 9.2 million hectares (23 million acres), with 55 percent occupied by cereal farming.
More than 90 percent of the cereal land was in the rainbelt. The Agriculture Ministry plans to increase irrigated land to 1.33 million hectares (3.3 million acres) by the year 2020, MAP said.
